note: Golden interoperability vectors for the Cauce V3 PTY channel. The gateway (TypeScript), the terminal-relay (TypeScript) and the pty-agent (Python 3 stdlib) must all reproduce these byte for byte. Do not 'recompute a better value': a mismatch is a protocol divergence, not a stale fixture.

geometry.note: One clamp for the four legs. The console only declares the maxima; the minima are enforced by the other three. Python is cited by module and constant name, never by line: the agent is a package and line numbers rot on the next split.

limits.note: Byte and cardinality ceilings of the channel. Every value is the constant the pty-agent enforces, except stdin_coalesce_ms, which only the relay owns.

ttls.note: Deadlines in seconds. The first three live in the agent; the last two are the deployed environment of gateway and relay.

modes.note: The three session modes and the gates that differ between them. `read_only` is EXACTLY {harness} and does not change: it is the set whose STDIN the agent discards before touching the descriptor. `writable` is the set whose STDIN reaches the pty. `tui` is the set allowed to send TERMINAL_RESPONSE, the DA/DSR answer the emulator owes the remote TUI; today both implementations write that gate with the OPPOSITE polarity -- `mode not in READ_ONLY_MODES` in the agent and `mode !== 'harness'` in the relay -- so a writable TUI mode would silently lose the channel its TUI needs to render. harness_rw is tui and writable at once, which is why those two sets overlap on it and only on it. Only `read_only` is bound to an implementation today: vectors.test.ts re-reads READ_ONLY_MODES out of session.py and compares it with this array, so the two cannot drift apart. `all` is a forward declaration and nothing enforces it yet: the agent's MODES tuple still lists two modes, and the relay narrows a hello to shell|harness -- one entry outside that pair invalidates the WHOLE hello and disconnects the agent -- so advertising harness_rw to the real relay today does not enable a writable TUI, it drops the leg. Widening both is a later task and this block is the declaration it lands against. Python is cited by module and constant, never by line.

sources.all: declared here first; the two places that must widen are ops/pty-agent/cauce_pty_agent/framing.py:MODES and services/terminal-relay/src/agent-hello.ts:modesField, both still shell|harness
